sections.html:
Westerville is a northeast suburb of Columbus that straddles two counties, Franklin and Delaware. That split decides which auditor, which board of revision and which health district you deal with. Population is about 38,165, down from 39,190 in 2020. The city runs its own electric and water utilities and collects no property tax at all.

The sections below start with where your parcel sits, then go through city steps, county filings and state paperwork for a sale.

For 2020 to 2024 the picture is a mid-priced suburb with a settled owner base.

  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 72.5%.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $374,500.
  • Median monthly owner costs: $2,120 with a mortgage and $968 without one.
  • Median gross rent: $1,364.
  • Households: 15,208, at 2.43 people per household.
  • Median household income: $109,404.

Interstates 71 and 270 border the city, State Route 3 runs through Uptown as State Street, and central Westerville is about 16 miles from downtown Columbus and 12 miles from John Glenn Columbus International Airport by interstate. Otterbein University and the Uptown district anchor the older part of town.

The city sits across the Franklin and Delaware county line, so start with the auditor's parcel search to see which county bills your house. The Franklin County Auditor's office is at 614-525-4663 and the Delaware County Auditor's office is at 740-833-2900.

Delaware's board reviews value as of the January 1 lien date and doesn't hear complaints about taxes. Hearings usually take 10 to 20 minutes, and an appeal goes to the Ohio Board of Tax Appeals or the county Court of Common Pleas within 30 days of the decision letter.

The Building Division is a state-certified department inside Planning and Development, reachable at 614-901-6650. It reviews plans before work starts and issues a Certificate of Occupancy or a Final Approval after inspections. Permit fees are paid when you pick up the permit, and plans go in through the city's Plan Review Portal.

  • Permits cover new buildings, alterations, signs, fences, pools, patio covers, decks, garages and satellite dishes, and fences carry no permit fee.
  • The city doesn't require a homeowner or contractor to hold a city license before pulling a permit.
  • A home occupation can need a conditional use permit.

Ask the division for your permit history before you list, and close out any permit that never received a final approval.

Westerville supplies electric and water service itself, while sewer treatment comes through Columbus and refuse through Rumpke. All four charges appear on one bill that is due on the 15th of the month after it is issued. Utility Billing sits at 21 S. State Street and answers at 614-901-6430. Sewer charges follow water use.

  • Refuse and recycling go out every Tuesday, and yard waste goes out every Monday.
  • Large items such as stoves and furniture can go to the curb on collection day, but air conditioners and refrigerators must go through outside vendors.
  • Owners must keep yards and vacant lots free of trash, debris, overgrown grass and weeds. Code Enforcement takes calls at 614-901-6650.
  • A garage sale needs no permit, but it is limited to one every six months and three consecutive days.

Schedule the final meter reading with Utility Billing as part of the closing checklist so the buyer's service starts clean.

Winter showings run into city rules. Plows clear all city streets once snow passes two inches, and a snow emergency starts automatically above three inches, after which cars left on the street can be towed. Owners must keep the walkway in front of the house clear of snow and ice.

The city removes fallen limbs from street trees, but a tree or branch that comes down from private property is the owner's job to remove. Westerville also offers free residential fire inspections at 614-901-6600, a quick safety check before a buyer's inspector arrives.

sections.h2: What an Ohio seller must deliver
sections.html:
Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 applies to sales of homes with one to four units. The seller completes the state disclosure form and delivers a signed copy to the buyer or the buyer's agent. Receiving it late opens a short rescission window, so hand it over before the offer is signed.

Value disputes follow ORC 5715.19. The complaint is due by March 31 of the next year, or the first-half collection closing date if that falls later.

sections.h2: Steps for a quick Westerville sale
sections.html:
Start by learning which county your parcel is in, because that sets the auditor you call, the board of revision you'd use and the health district that serves the house. Then pull the permit history from the Building Division and close out anything that never got a final approval. Open permits are one of the easiest things for a buyer's lender to catch late.

Next, get the yard and walkways in order, since Code Enforcement can act on overgrown grass, trash and debris. Book the final meter reading with Utility Billing for the closing date. Finally, complete the state disclosure form and hand it over before the offer is signed.

A cash buyer who accepts the house as-is can shorten the schedule, because there's no lender appraisal to wait on. Every one of the steps above still applies, though, and doing them early lets you accept a fast closing date without scrambling.

If you think the county value is too high, the timing matters as much as the evidence. Franklin County's filing season and Delaware County's window both close March 31, and Delaware accepts complaints starting January 2. Bring photos, repair estimates or a recent purchase agreement to the hearing, which usually runs 10 to 20 minutes. Remember that the board decides value only, so a complaint about the tax bill itself goes nowhere. Landlords selling a rental should confirm the registration with the auditor before closing, since the county tracks owner contact details and the buyer will need to update them.

faqs.q: Does the City of Westerville collect property taxes?
faqs.a: No. County governments collect property taxes for every taxing district. Call the Franklin County Auditor at 614-525-4663 or the Delaware County Auditor at 740-833-2900, depending on where your parcel sits.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to build a fence before I sell a Westerville house?
faqs.a: Yes, a permit is required to build, replace, relocate or alter a fence, though the city charges no permit fee. Call the Zoning Division at 614-901-6662.

faqs.q: Who collects trash at a Westerville house?
faqs.a: Refuse and recycling are collected Tuesdays and yard waste Mondays, and Rumpke provides refuse service. Containers go out no earlier than 6 p.m. the evening before and no later than 7 a.m. on collection day.

faqs.q: What is Westerville's income tax rate?
faqs.a: The city rate is 2.00%, and all adult residents and businesses file city returns. Ask the city's tax office at 614-901-6420 how a sale affects your filing.

faqs.q: How do I find out which county my Westerville house is in?
faqs.a: Search the parcel on either county auditor's website, or look at the property tax bill. Franklin and Delaware counties run separate boards of revision, health districts and auditor offices.
